ALUSI:94:6/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون تكريراً للجملة السابقة لتقرير معناها وفي النفوس

ALUSI:94:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r2.claim: On the fresh-promise reading, the ease may mean relief available in the caliphs' days or ease in the afterlife.
ALUSI:94:6/r2.anchor: بيد أن المراد باليسر هنا ما تيسر لهم في أيام الخلفاء أو يسر الآخرة

ALUSI:94:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r3.claim: The fresh-promise analysis is a syntactic resumption; such separation without waw is common, so no special explanation for the missing conjunction is needed.
ALUSI:94:6/r3.anchor: واحتمال الاستئناف هو الراجح لما علم من فضل التأسيس على التأكيد

ALUSI:94:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r4.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:94:6/r4.claim: Isam al-Din suggests that separation may be artful because the independent clause takes the form of a repetition; Al-Ālūsī answers that resumption already accounts for it.
ALUSI:94:6/r4.anchor: وقال عصام الدين لا يبعد أن تكون نكتة الفصل كونه في صورة التكرير

ALUSI:94:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r5.claim: The indefinite noun is used for magnification; it may also signal a new assurance, since repeating an indefinite suggests a different instance and contrast between hardship and ease.
ALUSI:94:6/r5.anchor: إلا أنه أوثر التنكير التفخيم وقد يقال إن فائدته الظهور في التأسيس

ALUSI:94:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:94:6/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Prophet came out delighted and laughing, saying one hardship would not overcome two eases, then recited these assurances. No grading is given.
ALUSI:94:6/r6.anchor: عن الحسن قال خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرحاً مسروراً وهو يضحك ويقول لن يغلب عسر يسرين

ALUSI:94:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r7.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI:94:6/r7.claim: A scholar says the clause confirms the preceding blessings and promises the Prophet that every difficulty will be made easy.
ALUSI:94:6/r7.anchor: وأفاد بعض الأجلة أن الكلام تقرير لما قبله وعدة له صلى الله عليه وسلم بتيسير كل عسير

ALUSI:94:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r8.claim: On this explanation, fa is causal though it precedes the cause: mentioning either hardship or ease calls the other to mind; the definite article generalizes hardship and the indefinite ease is magnified.
ALUSI:94:6/r8.anchor: فالفاء قيل سيبية ودخلت على السبب وان تعارف دخولها على المسبب لتسبب ذكره عن ذكره

ALUSI:94:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r9.claim: The generic hardship includes distress such as constricted breast, the burden, and obscurity; corresponding great ease includes expansion, relief, and raised remembrance, so one should not despair of God's relief.
ALUSI:94:6/r9.anchor: كأنه قيل فعلنا لك كذا وكذا لأن مع كل عسر كضيق الصدر والوزر المنقض للظهر والخمول

ALUSI:94:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:94:6/r10.claim: Another commentator takes fa as inferential, deriving a general rule from particular cases, like inferring that all animals move the lower jaw because humans, horses, and sheep do so when chewing.
ALUSI:94:6/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم الفاء للتفريع وهو من قبيل تفريع الحكم على الدليل في صورة الاستدلال بالجزئي على الكلي

ALUSI:94:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r11.claim: The second sentence has the same alternatives, and a fresh promise remains preferable; if hardship is one while ease is reiterated, the two great eases apparently mean worldly and afterlife relief.
ALUSI:94:6/r11.anchor: وفي الجملة الثانية الاحتمالان السابقان والاستئناف أيضاً هو الراجح لما تقدم

ALUSI:94:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:94:6/r12.claim: Some take the second sentence as repetition for emphasis, with the same hardship and ease both times, like repeating that a horseman has a spear.
ALUSI:94:6/r12.anchor: وقيل الظاهر أن الجملة الثانية تكرير للأولى وتأكيد لها فاليسر فيها عين اليسر في الأولى

ALUSI:94:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r13.claim: The saying about one hardship and two eases does not prove a distinct second promise: emphatic repetition can magnify one ease until it encompasses relief in both worlds.
ALUSI:94:6/r13.anchor: ولن يغلب عسر يسرين ليس نصاً في الحمل على الاستئناف إذ يصح على التأكيد أيضاً

ALUSI:94:6/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI:94:6/r14.claim: The second sentence is absent from Ibn Masud's codex, although the saying about one hardship and two eases is also transmitted from him; this weakens the claim that the saying proves two distinct eases.
ALUSI:94:6/r14.anchor: أنه ليس في مصحف ابن مسعود الجملة الثانية مع أنه جاء عنه أيضاً لن يغلب عسر يسرين

ALUSI:94:6/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:94:6/r15.claim: A further proposal says one hardship cannot overcome the ease mentioned twice in a consoling promise; Al-Ālūsī dismisses this construal as strained.
ALUSI:94:6/r15.anchor: وقيل يمكن أن يحمل الخبر على أنه لن يغلب فرد من أفراد العسر ذكر اليسر مرتين

ALUSI:94:6/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r16.claim: The familiar explanation treats maʿa, accompaniment, as a metaphor for baʿda, after: their closeness exaggerates how promptly ease follows hardship.
ALUSI:94:6/r16.anchor: والمشهور على جميع الأوجه أنه شبه التقارب بالتقارن فاستعير لفظ مع لمعنى بعد

ALUSI:94:6/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r17.claim: Generic hardship seems problematic because lasting illness or poverty may have no worldly sequel, and a disbeliever's hardship may have no afterlife ease; the consoling judgment is understood for believers.
ALUSI:94:6/r17.anchor: واستشكل أمر الاستغراق بأن من العسر ما لا يعقبه يسر دنيوي كالفقر والمرض الدائمين إلى الموت

ALUSI:94:6/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r18.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI:94:6/r18.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that Abu Ubayda wrote Umar about Roman forces; Umar replied that distress falling on a believer is followed by relief. Al-Ālūsī says the report does not resolve every case.
ALUSI:94:6/r18.anchor: ما رواه مالك في الموطأ عن زيد بن أسلم قال كتب أبو عبيدة إلى عمر بن الخطاب

ALUSI:94:6/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r19.claim: Even restricting the promise to believers leaves hardships without worldly relief, and an impatient believer may receive no afterlife reward; a patient-only reading still leaves difficulty.
ALUSI:94:6/r19.anchor: إذ يبقى معه إن من عسر المؤمن ما لا يعقبه يسر دنيوي كما هو ظاهر

ALUSI:94:6/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r20.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:94:6/r20.claim: On the emphatic reading, some answer that generic scope is conventional and hardship is usually followed by ease; on a fresh-promise reading, they add that it concerns a patient believer.
ALUSI:94:6/r20.anchor: وأجاب بعض على وجه التأكيد بأن الاستغراق عرفي ويكفي فيه أن العسر في الغالب

ALUSI:94:6/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r21.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:94:6/r21.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet told his companions that two hardships would not overcome two eases, God willing; this supplies a condition not explicit in the verse.
ALUSI:94:6/r21.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال ذكر لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذه الآية أصحابه

ALUSI:94:6/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r22.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI:94:6/r22.claim: Some allow literal accompaniment: every hardship has at least some ease, such as God's averting something worse; magnified ease is prevention of greater harm.
ALUSI:94:6/r22.anchor: يفهم من كلام بعض الأفاضل أنه يجوز على وجه التأكيد أن يكون مع على ظاهرها

ALUSI:94:6/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r23.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI:94:6/r23.claim: Under literal accompaniment, the two eases may be one ease mentioned twice or immediate assurance plus customary later relief; the argument may also invoke 65:7 if revealed earlier.
ALUSI:94:6/r23.anchor: وأنه لا يأبى ذلك لن يغلب عسر يسرين اما لأن المعنى لن يغلب فرد

ALUSI:94:6/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r24.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:94:6/r24.claim: Some elect mystics say accompaniment is literal because everything the Beloved does is beloved; Ibn al-Farid and an anonymous Persian poet depict lovers savoring harsh treatment. Al-Ālūsī rejects this.
ALUSI:94:6/r24.anchor: وذكر بعضم ان المعية على حقيقتها عند الخاصة على معنى ان كل ما فعل المحبوب محبوب

ALUSI:94:6/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r25.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI:94:6/r25.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said ease would enter a stone to drive hardship out, then recited the verse; Al-Ālūsī says this makes literal accompaniment unlikely. No grading is stated.
ALUSI:94:6/r25.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالساً وحياله حجر فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام لو جاء العسر

ALUSI:94:6/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI:94:6/r26.claim: Reading al-ʿusr as a known hardship avoids objections and suits the occasion report, but the apparent rhetoric favors generality; then the promise is conditioned on trust, hope, and reliance on God.
ALUSI:94:6/r26.anchor: وإرادة العهد أسلم من القيل والقال وكأن من اختاره اختاره لذلك مع الاستئناس له بسبب النزول

ALUSI:94:6/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:94:6/r27.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو جعفر وعيسى
ALUSI:94:6/r27.claim: Ibn Waththab, Abu Jafar, and Isa read al-ʿusr and yusran in both occurrences with a damma on the sīn.
ALUSI:94:6/r27.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وأبو جعفر وعيسى العسر ويسرا في الموضعين بضم السين

BAGHAWI:94:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:94:6/r1.claim: God promised ease and prosperity after hardship: while the Prophet was distressed in Mecca, He promised relief from the struggle against the polytheists through victory and their submission to the truth.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r1.anchor: ثم وعده اليسر والرخاء بعد الشدة ، وذلك أنه كان بمكة في شدة

BAGHAWI:94:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:94:6/r2.claim: Repeating the promise confirms it and magnifies hope.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r2.anchor: { إن مع العسر يسرا } كرره لتأكيد الوعد وتعظيم الرجاء

BAGHAWI:94:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:94:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that after this verse was revealed the Prophet gave glad tidings: one hardship will not overcome two eases.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن لما نزلت هذه الآية قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " أبشروا ، قد جاءكم اليسر

BAGHAWI:94:6/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI:94:6/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that if hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it out and enter; one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r4.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : لو كان العسر في جحر لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه

BAGHAWI:94:6/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r5.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI:94:6/r5.claim: The exegetes explain that repeating definite al-ʿusr refers to the same hardship, while repeating indefinite yusr refers to two distinct eases; they illustrate the rule with repeated use of “a dirham” versus “the dirham.”
BAGHAWI:94:6/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون : ومعنى قوله : " لن يغلب عسر يسرين " أن الله تعالى كرر العسر بلفظ المعرفة واليسر بلفظ النكرة

BAGHAWI:94:6/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r6.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
BAGHAWI:94:6/r6.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Jurjani rejects the definiteness argument as inadequate: repeating “with the horse a sword” would not entail one horse but two swords.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني صاحب النظم : تكلم الناس في قوله : " لن يغلب عسر يسرين " فلم يحصل

BAGHAWI:94:6/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:94:6/r8.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
BAGHAWI:94:6/r8.claim: Jurjani reads the second, uncoordinated promise as lasting afterlife ease for all believers; worldly hardship cannot defeat both it and worldly ease, since afterlife ease endures, like two feast months do not both fall short.
BAGHAWI:94:6/r8.anchor: ثم ابتدأ فضلاً آخر من أمر الآخرة ، فقال : إن مع العسر يسراً ، والدليل على ابتدائه : تعريه من الفاء والواو

BAYDAWI:94:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:6/r1.claim: The repetition may emphasize the assurance or promise that hardship will be followed by another ease, such as the fasting person's joy at breaking fast and at meeting the Lord.
BAYDAWI:94:6/r1.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد أو استئناف وعده بأن العسر متبوع بيسر آخر كثواب الآخرة

BAYDAWI:94:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:6/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:94:6/r2.claim: A prophetic saying states that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
BAYDAWI:94:6/r2.anchor: وعليه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لن يغلب عسر يسرين "

BAYDAWI:94:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:94:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:94:6/r3.claim: The definite al-ʿusr refers to the same hardship whether definite by reference or by generic use; the indefinite yusr can denote a second, different ease.
BAYDAWI:94:6/r3.anchor: فإن العسر معرف فلا يتعدد سواء كان للعهد أو للجنس ، واليسر منكر فيحتمل أن يراد بالثاني فرد يغاير ما أريد بالأول

BIQAI:94:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r1.claim: Hardship is painful, and its great divine purposes are visible only to exceptional servants; repeating the promise reassures and encourages people to face it.
BIQAI:94:6/r1.anchor: ولما كان العسر مكروهاً إلى النفوس ، وكان لله سبحانه وتعالى فيه حكماً عظيمة ، وكانت الحكم لا تتراءى إلا للأفراد من العباد

BIQAI:94:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r2.claim: The repeated assurance answers the imagined question, “Will hardship be followed by more hardship?”, and reinforces hope.
BIQAI:94:6/r2.anchor: على طريق الاستئناف لجواب من يقول : وهل بعده من عسر ؟ مؤكداً له ترغيباً في أمره

BIQAI:94:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r3.claim: Biqāʿī reads the definite hardship as the same hardship, while allowing each indefinite ease to denote a distinct ease; this yields one hardship and two eases.
BIQAI:94:6/r3.anchor: مبشراً بتكريره مع وحدة العسر وإن كان حمل كل واحد منهما على شيء غير ما قصد به الآخر ممكناً

BIQAI:94:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r4.claim: The customary grammatical principle is that a repeated indefinite is different, whereas a repeated definite refers back to the same thing.
BIQAI:94:6/r4.anchor: وقد اشتهر أن النكرة إذا أعيدت نكرة فالثاني غير الأول ، والمعرفة بالعكس

BIQAI:94:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:94:6/r5.claim: The Prophet reportedly clarifies that the second ease is distinct from the first.
BIQAI:94:6/r5.anchor: وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  إنها غيرُها  "

BIQAI:94:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
BIQAI:94:6/r6.claim: Al-Hasan al-Baṣrī reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said that ease had come and one hardship would not overcome two eases.
BIQAI:94:6/r6.anchor: فقال الحسن البصري : إن الآية لما نزلت قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  أتاكم اليسر لن يغلب عسر يسرين  "

BIQAI:94:6/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI:94:6/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that even if hardship were inside a lizard’s hole, ease would pursue it and drive it out; ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmits this as his saying.
BIQAI:94:6/r7.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال :  "  لو كان العسر في جحر ضب لتبعه اليسر حتى يخرجه  "

BIQAI:94:6/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:94:6/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits from Ibn Masʿūd a prophetic version: ease would enter even a hole containing hardship and bring it out.
BIQAI:94:6/r8.anchor: ثم قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الآية

BIQAI:94:6/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r9.speaker: نور الدين الهيثمي
BIQAI:94:6/r9.claim: Al-Haythamī grades the Ṭabarānī report from Ibn Masʿūd weak because its chain contains Abū Mālik al-Nakhaʿī.
BIQAI:94:6/r9.anchor: قال الحافظ نور الدين الهيثمي : وفيه أبو مالك النخعي وهو ضعيف

BIQAI:94:6/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r10.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
BIQAI:94:6/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bazzār transmit a similar report from Anas; al-Haythamī calls its chain weak because it contains ʿĀʾidh ibn Shurayḥ.
BIQAI:94:6/r10.anchor: والبزار عن أنس رضي الله عنه بنحوه ، قال الهيثمي : وفيه عائذ بن شريح وهو ضعيف

BIQAI:94:6/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:94:6/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet once came out laughing and repeated that one hardship would not overcome two eases.
BIQAI:94:6/r11.anchor: وروى الفراء عن الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج ذات يوم وهو يضحك ويقول :  "  لن يغلب عسر يسرين  "

BIQAI:94:6/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r12.speaker: الحسن البصري
BIQAI:94:6/r12.claim: The same saying is transmitted from al-Hasan as a mursal report by ʿAbd al-Razzāq; al-Ḥākim, al-Bayhaqī, and al-Ṭabarī also transmit it, while Ibn Mardawayh’s connected route is weak.
BIQAI:94:6/r12.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن أيوب عن الحسن به مرسلاً ، ومن طريقه أخرجه الحاكم والبيهقي في الشعب

BIQAI:94:6/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r13.speaker: عمر
BIQAI:94:6/r13.claim: ʿUmar reportedly received word that Abū ʿUbayda, then in Syria, sent him a letter repeating that one hardship would not overcome two eases.
BIQAI:94:6/r13.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه بلغه أن أبا عبيدة رضي الله عنه حضر بالشام فكتب إليه كتاباً فيه

BIQAI:94:6/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r14.speaker: ابن حجر
BIQAI:94:6/r14.claim: Ibn Ḥajar calls the route for ʿUmar’s report the soundest of these routes.
BIQAI:94:6/r14.anchor: قال ذلك شيخنا ابن حجر في تخريج أحاديث الكشاف ، وقال : وهذا أصح طرقه

BIQAI:94:6/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r15.speaker: سعد الدين التفتازاني
BIQAI:94:6/r15.claim: Al-Taftāzānī divides repetition into four cases based on whether the first and second expressions are definite or indefinite, and says to judge identity by the second form.
BIQAI:94:6/r15.anchor: قال الشيخ سعد الدين التفتازاني في أول تلويحه في الكلام على المعرفة والنكرة : الكلام فيما إذا أعيد اللفظ الأول

BIQAI:94:6/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r16.speaker: الكشاف
BIQAI:94:6/r16.claim: Al-Kashshāf argues that repeating an indefinite yields a different referent because an indefinite selects only part of a genus.
BIQAI:94:6/r16.anchor: وذكر في الكشف أنه إذا أعيدت النكرة نكرة فالثاني مغاير للأول لكان بعينه

BIQAI:94:6/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r17.claim: Biqāʿī objects that definiteness need not be generic: anaphoric reference is the default, and prior mention does not force a following indefinite to identify the same thing.
BIQAI:94:6/r17.anchor: أما أولاً فلأن التعريف لا يلزم أن تكون للاستغراق بل العهد هو الأصل ، وعند تقدم المعهود لا يلزم أن تكون النكرة عينه

BIQAI:94:6/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r18.claim: A part included in a whole is not thereby the same intended referent, so the part-versus-whole explanation cannot establish identity.
BIQAI:94:6/r18.anchor: وأما ثانياً فلأن معنى كون الثاني عين الأول أن يكون المراد به هو المراد بالأول ، والجزء بالنسبة إلى الكل ليس كذلك

BIQAI:94:6/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r19.claim: The Qurʾān often repeats a definite expression as an indefinite with a different referent; examples include the book, an enemy, and degrees.
BIQAI:94:6/r19.anchor: وأما ثالثاً فإن إعادة المعرفة نكرة مع مغايرة الثاني للأول كثير في الكلام ، قال الله تعالى

BIQAI:94:6/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r20.claim: An anonymous poet’s line about people and time shows that repeating an expression with the same referent would add no information.
BIQAI:94:6/r20.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر : إذا الناس ناس والزمان زمان *** فإن الثاني لو كان عين الأول لم يكن في الإخبار به فائدة - انتهى

BIQAI:94:6/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r21.claim: Context can also make a repeated indefinite refer to the same thing, as in these Qurʾānic examples and in verbal emphasis.
BIQAI:94:6/r21.anchor: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله

BIQAI:94:6/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r22.claim: A first indefinite can be followed by a definite that has a different, more specific referent, as in the cited examples of scripture, reconciliation, and added punishment.
BIQAI:94:6/r22.anchor: وقد تعاد النكرة معرفة مع المغايرة كقوله تعالى :

BIQAI:94:6/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r23.claim: Repeated definite expressions can also differ in reference: the cited examples distinguish scriptures, kinds of sovereignty, reward, and killer from victim.
BIQAI:94:6/r23.anchor: وقد تعاد المعرفة معرفة مع المغايرة كقوله تعالى :

BIQAI:94:6/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r24.claim: Conversely, a definite may be repeated as an indefinite without changing its referent, as in the declaration that God is one deity.
BIQAI:94:6/r24.anchor: وقد تعاد المعرفة نكرة مع عدم المغايرة كقوله تعالى :

BIQAI:94:6/r25.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:94:6/r25.speaker: author
BIQAI:94:6/r25.claim: Biqāʿī treats identity for repeated definites and difference for repeated indefinites as defaults that hold absent contextual clues, then applies this to the verse’s definite hardship and indefinite ease.
BIQAI:94:6/r25.anchor: أي العسر الذي أنتم عليه أو الجنس أي الذي يعرفه كل أحد

DURR:94:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:94:6/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { فإن مع العسر يسراً } قال : اتبع العسر يسراً

DURR:94:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:94:6/r2.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet gave his companions glad tidings from this verse, saying one hardship will not overcome two eases.
DURR:94:6/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { فإن مع العسر يسراً إن مع العسر يسراً } قال : ذكر لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:94:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR:94:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet announced that ease had come and one hardship would not overcome two eases.
DURR:94:6/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إن مع العسر يسراً } قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «أبشروا

DURR:94:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR:94:6/r4.claim: Jabir recounts an expedition of at least 300 under Abu Ubayda with little food: after they asked for more provisions, the Prophet sent glad tidings that hardship cannot overcome two eases.
DURR:94:6/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : «بعثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن ثلثمائة أو يزيدون ، علينا أبو عبيدة بن الجراح

DURR:94:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:94:6/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that if hardship entered a stone, ease would follow it inside and drive it out; the verse was revealed.
DURR:94:6/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالساً وحياله حجر ، فقال : «لو جاء العسر

DURR:94:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:94:6/r6.claim: A second report from Anas places the saying at Baqi al-Farqad: ease would enter a stone after hardship and drive it out, followed by the verse's revelation.
DURR:94:6/r6.anchor: عن عائذ عن أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان قاعداً ببقيع الفرقد ، فنزل إلى حائط

DURR:94:6/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:94:6/r7.claim: A weak-chain report from Ibn Mas'ud has the Prophet say that if hardship were inside a stone, ease would enter and remove it, then recite the verse.
DURR:94:6/r7.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن ابن مسعود قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «لو كان العسر في حجر لدخل عليه اليسر

DURR:94:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:94:6/r8.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says ease would pursue hardship even into a stone to remove it, and that one hardship cannot overcome two eases, as God says in the repeated verse.
DURR:94:6/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : لو كان العسر في حجر لتبعه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه ليخرجه ، ولن يغلب عسر يسرين

DURR:94:6/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR:94:6/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reports the Prophet once came out joyful and laughing, saying hardship would not overcome two eases and reciting the repeated verse.
DURR:94:6/r9.anchor: عن الحسن قال : خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوماً فرحاً مسروراً ، وهو يضحك ويقول : «لن يغلب عسر يسرين

DURR:94:6/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:94:6/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR:94:6/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says people used to say one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
DURR:94:6/r10.anchor: عن الحسن قال : كانوا يقولون : لا يغلب عسر واحد يسرين اثنين

IBNASHUR:94:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r1.claim: The second sentence repeats and confirms the first to establish the regular, universal fulfillment of this remarkable promise.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r1.anchor: وجملة :  { إن مع العسر يسراً } مؤكدة لجملة :  { فإن مع العسر يسراً } وفائدة هذا التأكيد تحقيق اطراد هذا الوعد

IBNASHUR:94:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r2.speaker: من المفسرين
IBNASHUR:94:6/r2.claim: Some commentators assign worldly ease to the first sentence and afterlife ease to the second.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r2.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل اليسر في الجملة الأولى يسر الدنيا وفي الجملة الثانية يسر الآخرة

IBNASHUR:94:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects that division because Arabic syntax makes the second sentence a pure confirmation.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r3.anchor: وأسلوب الكلام العربي لا يساعد عليه لأنه متمحض لكون الثانية تأكيداً

IBNASHUR:94:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:94:6/r4.claim: The Prophet's saying that one hardship will not overcome two eases is linked in wording and meaning to this verse; some reports say he recited it, and exegetes widely derive the saying from it.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r4.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « لن يغلب عسر يسرين »

IBNASHUR:94:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r5.speaker: شاع بين أهل العلم
IBNASHUR:94:6/r5.claim: A common explanation says repeated definite al-usri denotes the same hardship, while repeated indefinite yusr denotes two different eases.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r5.anchor: وشاع بين أهل العلم أن ذلك مستفاد من تعريف كلمة العسر وإعادتها معرفة ومن تنكير كملة « يسر » وإعادتها منكَّرة

IBNASHUR:94:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects this grammatical proof: its rule concerns an indefinite reintroduced as definite with a definite article of reference, and separate sentences; here the definite is generic and the sentence is repeated.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r6.anchor: وبناء كلامهم على قاعدة إعادة النكرة معرفة خطأ لأن تلك القاعدة في إعادة النكرة معرفة لا في إعادة المعرفة معرفة

IBNASHUR:94:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r7.speaker: أبو علي الحسين الجرجاني
IBNASHUR:94:6/r7.claim: Abu Ali al-Husayn al-Jurjani had previously refuted this grammatical argument in his book al-Nazm.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r7.anchor: وقد أبطله من قبل أبو علي الحسين الجرجاني{[454]} في كتاب « النظم »

IBNASHUR:94:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف وابن هشام
IBNASHUR:94:6/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf also rejects the argument, and Ibn Hisham calls the rule erroneous.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r8.anchor: وأبطله صاحب « الكشاف » أيضاً ،  وجعل ابن هشام في « مغني اللبيب » تلك القاعدة خطأ

IBNASHUR:94:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r9.claim: The repeated sentence strengthens the judgment that ease accompanies hardship, and thus makes ease's effect outweigh hardship's.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r9.anchor: والذي يظهر في تقرير معنى قوله :  « لن يغلب عسر يسرين » أن جملة :  { إن مع العسر يسراً } تأكيد لجملة

IBNASHUR:94:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r10.claim: Two eases is a symbolic metonym for dominance: dual forms can signify repeated abundance, as in repeated looking and Arabic expressions such as labbayk.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r10.anchor: فالتثنية هنا كناية رمزية عن التغلب والرجحان فإن التثنية قد يكنى بها عن التكرير المراد منه التكثير

IBNASHUR:94:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:94:6/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:94:6/r11.claim: The saying about two eases does not derive from the definite article on hardship or the repeated indefinite form of ease.
IBNASHUR:94:6/r11.anchor: وليس ذلك مستفاداً من تعريف { العسر } باللام ولا من تنكير « اليسر » وإعادته منكراً

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r1.claim: God strengthens the Prophet’s hope: alongside the harm he sees, relief will come.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r1.anchor: أي مع ما تراه من الأذى فرج يأتيك

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r2.claim: God repeats the promise to emphasize it and clarify the coming good.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r2.anchor: وكرر الله تعالى ذلك مبالغة وتبيينا للخير

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r3.claim: Some say one ease accompanies hardship in this world and another in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r3.anchor: فقال بعض الناس : المعنى  إن مع العسر يسرا في الدنيا وإن مع العسر يسرا في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r4.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r4.claim: Many scholars hold that each hardship comes with two eases.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r4.anchor: وذهب كثير من العلماء إلى أن مع كل عسر يسرين بهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r5.claim: He explains the two eases as distinct because hardship is definite while ease is indefinite.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r5.anchor: من حيث  " العسر "  معرف للعهد ،   و " اليسر " منكر ،   فالأول غير الثاني

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says that one hardship will not overcome two eases; Ibn ʿAṭiyya states no grading.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r6.anchor: وقد روي في هذا التأويل حديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r7.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r7.claim: ʿUmar states this interpretation in his letter to Abū ʿUbayda in the Muwaṭṭaʾ.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r7.anchor: وأما قول عمر به فنص في الموطأ في رسالته إلى أبي عبيدة بن الجراح

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r8.speaker: عيسى ويحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r8.claim: ʿĪsā, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and Abū Jaʿfar read both words with ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r8.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ويحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر : ( العسر واليسر ) بضمتين

IBNATIYYA:94:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the clause once, without its repetition.
IBNATIYYA:94:6/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : [ إن مع العسر يسرا ] واحدة غير مكررة

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r1.claim: God states that ease exists alongside hardship and then reinforces this assurance by repeating it.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r1.anchor: أخبر تعالى أن مع العسر يوجَدُ اليسر ، ثم أكد هذا الخبر .

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said if hardship entered a rock, ease would follow into it and drive hardship out; the verse was revealed. Ibn Kathīr notes that Abū Ḥātim judged ʿĀʾidh ibn Shurayḥ's hadith weak, and al-Bazzār knew it only through him from Anas.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r2.anchor: حدثنا عائذ بن شريح قال : سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r3.claim: The maxim that one hardship cannot overcome two eases is also transmitted as a Companion statement from Ibn Masʿūd through Shuʿba, Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, and an unnamed intermediary.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r3.anchor: ولكن رواه شعبة عن معاوية بن قرة ، عن رجل ، عن عبد الله بن مسعود موقوفا .

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says people used to affirm that one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r4.anchor: حدثنا المبارك بن فضالة ، عن الحسن قال : كانوا يقولون : لا يغلب عسر واحد يسرين اثنين .

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r5.claim: A mursal report through al-Ḥasan says the Prophet came out joyful and laughing, repeating that one hardship would not overcome two eases; Ibn Jarīr also gives mursal routes through ʿAwf and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r5.anchor: عن معمر ، عن الحسن قال : خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما مسرورا فرحا وهو يضحك ، وهو يقول

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r6.claim: Qatāda says it was related that the Prophet gave his companions the glad tidings of this verse with the saying that one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد ، عن قتادة : ذُكِرَ لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بشر أصحابه بهذه الآية فقال

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r7.claim: Because al-ʿusr is definite in both clauses, it is one hardship; the indefinite yusr is repeated and thus denotes two eases, explaining the maxim.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r7.anchor: ومعنى هذا : أن العسر معرف في الحالين ، فهو مفرد ، واليسر منكر فتعدد

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that support descends from heaven in proportion to hardship and patience in proportion to calamity.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r9.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r9.claim: A poem attributed to al-Shāfiʿī says that patient trust in God brings survival and that hoped-for relief is near.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r9.anchor: ومما يروى عن الشافعي ، رضي الله عنه ، أنه قال : صبرا جميلا ما أقرب الفرجا *** من راقب الله في الأمور نجا

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r10.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r10.claim: A poem recited by Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī says that when despair and troubles seem settled, the Gentle, Responsive God sends aid, and relief follows when calamities reach their limit.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r10.anchor: وقال ابن دريد : أنشدني أبو حاتم السجستاني : إذا اشتملت على اليأس القلوبُ *** وضاق لما به الصدر الرحيبُ

IBNKATHIR:94:6/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r11.speaker: آخر
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r11.claim: An unattributed poem says that when a calamity tightens its grip, God provides a way out, and relief arrives after its rings are fully tightened.
IBNKATHIR:94:6/r11.anchor: وقال آخر : ولرب نازلة يضيق بها الفتى *** ذرعا وعند الله منها المخرج

MAWARDI:94:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r1.claim: One view links worldly striving with the good of the Hereafter.
MAWARDI:94:6/r1.anchor: إن مع اجتهاد الدنيا خير الآخرة

MAWARDI:94:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r2.claim: Another view says hardship comes with relief, patience with expansion, misery with happiness, and difficulty with ease.
MAWARDI:94:6/r2.anchor: الثاني : إن مع الشدة رخاء ، ومع الصبر سعة ، ومع الشقاوة سعادة ، ومع الحزونة سهولة

MAWARDI:94:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r3.claim: One possibility is that God holds hardship and ease together and may do as He wills with either.
MAWARDI:94:6/r3.anchor: أن مع العسر يسرا عند الله ليفعل منهما ما شاء

MAWARDI:94:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r4.claim: Another possibility is that worldly hardship comes with ease in the Hereafter.
MAWARDI:94:6/r4.anchor: إن مع العسر في الدنيا يسرا في الآخرة

MAWARDI:94:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r5.claim: For someone tested, hardship comes with ease for the one who is patient and seeks reward, through contentment or provision.
MAWARDI:94:6/r5.anchor: إن مع العسر لمن بلي يسرا لمن صبر واحتسب بما يوفق له من القناعة أو بما يعطى من السعة

MAWARDI:94:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:94:6/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd swears that even if hardship were inside a stone, ease would seek it out and enter; hardship will not overcome two eases.
MAWARDI:94:6/r6.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : والذي نفسي بيده لو كان العسر في حَجَرٍ لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه

MAWARDI:94:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:94:6/r7.claim: The two occurrences of hardship refer to one hardship because both have the definite article, while the two eases are distinct because ease is indefinite.
MAWARDI:94:6/r7.anchor: وإنما كان العسر في الموضعين واحداً ، واليسر اثنين ، لدخول الألف واللام على العسر وحذفها من اليسر

MAWARDI:94:6/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r8.speaker: ثعلب
MAWARDI:94:6/r8.claim: Thaʿlab says repeating the phrase distinguishes one hardship from two eases, strengthening hope and encouraging patience.
MAWARDI:94:6/r8.anchor: أحدهما : ما ذكرنا من إفراد العسر وتثنية اليسر ، ليكون أقوى للأمل وأبعث على الصبر ، قاله ثعلب

MAWARDI:94:6/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:94:6/r9.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI:94:6/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the repeated phrase as emphatic elaboration, like repeated yes/no replies; al-Māwardī also cites al-Khansāʾ’s repeated awlā.
MAWARDI:94:6/r9.anchor: الثاني : للإطناب والمبالغة ، كما قالوا في تكرار الجواب فيقال : بلى بلى ، لا لا ، قاله الفراء

NASAFI:94:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:6/r1.claim: The hardship is the Prophet's suffering under the polytheists' abuse; ease is God's making him prevail over them.
NASAFI:94:6/r1.anchor: أي إن مع الشدة التي أنت فيها من مقاساة بلاء المشركين يسراً بإظهاري إياك عليهم حتى تغلبهم

NASAFI:94:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:94:6/r2.claim: It is said the polytheists mocked the Prophet and believers for poverty, making him fear that poverty turned them from Islam.
NASAFI:94:6/r2.anchor: وقيل : كان المشركون يعيرون رسول الله والمؤمنين بالفقر حتى سبق إلى وهمه أنهم رغبوا عن الإسلام لافتقار أهله

NASAFI:94:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:6/r3.claim: God reminds him of His great gifts and says not to despair of divine grace.
NASAFI:94:6/r3.anchor: كأنه قال : خولناك ما خولناك فلا تيأس من فضل الله

NASAFI:94:6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:6/r4.claim: “With” expresses how closely ease accompanies hardship, consoling and strengthening hearts.
NASAFI:94:6/r4.anchor: وجيء بلفظ «مع » لغاية مقاربة اليسر العسر زيادة في التسلية ولتقوية القلوب

NASAFI:94:6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI:94:6/r5.claim: At its revelation the Prophet said, “No hardship will overcome two eases.”
NASAFI:94:6/r5.anchor: وإنما قال عليه السلام عند نزولها : " لن يغلب عسر يسرين "

NASAFI:94:6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:94:6/r6.claim: The repeated definite “hardship” denotes the same hardship, while the repeated indefinite “ease” denotes a second ease.
NASAFI:94:6/r6.anchor: لأن العسر أعيد معرفاً فكان واحداً ، لأن المعرفة إذا أعيدت معرفة كانت الثانية عين الأولى

NASAFI:94:6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:94:6/r7.speaker: أبو معاذ
NASAFI:94:6/r7.claim: Abu Muadh illustrates how repeated definite nouns refer to the same, while indefinite repeated nouns can refer to new ones.
NASAFI:94:6/r7.anchor: قال أبو معاذ : يقال إن مع الأمير غلاماً إن مع الأمير غلاماً

QURTUBI:94:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r1.claim: The hardship is constriction and difficulty; the ease is spaciousness and wealth.
QURTUBI:94:6/r1.anchor: أي إن مع الضيقة والشدة يسرا

QURTUBI:94:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:94:6/r2.claim: The repeated clause emphasizes and magnifies the promise, like repeated commands, repeated answers, Qur'an 102:3, and the poet's repeated appeal.
QURTUBI:94:6/r2.anchor: وذلك للإطناب والمبالغة . قاله الفراء . ومنه قول الشاعر :

QURTUBI:94:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r3.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI:94:6/r3.claim: In Arab usage, repeating a definite noun refers to the same thing, while repeating an indefinite noun refers to another; thus there are two eases, strengthening hope and patience.
QURTUBI:94:6/r3.anchor: وهما اثنان ، ليكون أقوى للأمل ، وأبعث على الصبر . قاله ثعلب .

QURTUBI:94:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:94:6/r4.claim: God created one hardship and two eases, so one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
QURTUBI:94:6/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : يقول الله تعالى خلقت عسرا واحدا ، وخلقت يسرين ، ولن يغلب عسر يسرين

QURTUBI:94:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:94:6/r5.claim: A report about this sura quotes the Prophet saying that one hardship will never overcome two eases; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
QURTUBI:94:6/r5.anchor: وجاء في الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه السورة : أنه قال : [ لن يغلب عسر يسرين ]

QURTUBI:94:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:94:6/r6.claim: Ibn Masud swears that even if hardship were inside a stone, ease would pursue it and enter; one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
QURTUBI:94:6/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود{[16173]} : والذي نفسي بيده ، لو كان العسر في حجر ، لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه

QURTUBI:94:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI:94:6/r7.claim: Replying to Abu Ubayda's concern about Roman forces, Umar assures him that a believer's hardship is followed by relief, cites this promise, and invokes 3:200.
QURTUBI:94:6/r7.anchor: فكتب إليه عمر رضي الله عنهما : أما بعد ، فإنه مهما ينزل بعبد مؤمن من منزل شدة ، يجعل الله بعده فرجا

QURTUBI:94:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r8.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI:94:6/r8.claim: Al-Jurjani rejects the definite-versus-indefinite argument as unsound: its logic would make two mentions of a horse and sword imply one horse but two swords.
QURTUBI:94:6/r8.anchor: وقال قوم منهم الجرجاني : هذا قول مدخول ؛ لأنه يجب على هذا التدريج إذا قال الرجل : إن مع الفارس سيفا

QURTUBI:94:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r9.claim: Qurtubi prefers a contextual reading: the poor Prophet was mocked for poverty, became distressed, and God consoled him by promising prompt worldly relief.
QURTUBI:94:6/r9.anchor: والصحيح أن يقال : إن الله بعث نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم مقلا مخفا ، فعيره المشركون بفقره

QURTUBI:94:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r10.claim: The worldly promise was fulfilled before the Prophet died: he conquered the Hijaz and Yemen, gained wealth, gave lavish gifts including 200 camels, and kept a year's provisions for his family.
QURTUBI:94:6/r10.anchor: فأنجز له ما وعده ، فلم يمت حتى فتح عليه الحجاز واليمن ، ووسع ذات يده ، حتى كان يعطي الرجل المائتين من الإبل

QURTUBI:94:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r11.claim: Although the first worldly favor was specific to the Prophet, some of his community may also receive it, God willing.
QURTUBI:94:6/r11.anchor: وإن كان خاصا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فقد يدخل فيه بعض أمته إن شاء الله تعالى

QURTUBI:94:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r12.claim: The second clause begins a new promise because it has no coordinating particle such as fa or waw to mark it as joined to the first.
QURTUBI:94:6/r12.anchor: والدليل على ابتدائه ، تعريه من فاء أو واو أو غيرها من حروف النسق التي تدل على العطف

QURTUBI:94:6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r13.claim: The second promise is for all believers: hardship in this world necessarily accompanies ease in the afterlife, though worldly and afterlife ease may also coincide.
QURTUBI:94:6/r13.anchor: فهذا وعد عام لجميع المؤمنين ، لا يخرج أحد منه ، أي إن مع العسر في الدنيا للمؤمنين يسرا في الآخرة لا محالة . وربما اجتمع يسر الدنيا

QURTUBI:94:6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r14.claim: The report that one hardship cannot overcome two eases means worldly ease might be overcome, but afterlife ease is certain and nothing can overcome it.
QURTUBI:94:6/r14.anchor: وإنما يغلب أحدهما إن غلب ، وهو يسر الدنيا ، فأما يسر الآخرة فكائن لا محالة ، ولن يغلبه شيء

QURTUBI:94:6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:94:6/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:94:6/r15.claim: Another interpretation makes the hardship the Prophet's expulsion from Mecca and the ease his honorable return at its conquest with ten thousand men.
QURTUBI:94:6/r15.anchor: وهو إخراج أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة

RAZI:94:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:94:6/r1.claim: Mockery of Muhammad's poverty distressed him; God recalls earlier favors and promises worldly relief, with the fā linking that promise to his distress.
RAZI:94:6/r1.anchor: لا يحزنك ما يقول وما أنت فيه من القلة

RAZI:94:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:94:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God created one hardship between two eases, so one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
RAZI:94:6/r2.anchor: خلقت عسرا واحدا بين يسرين ، فلن يغلب عسر يسرين

RAZI:94:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r3.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI:94:6/r3.claim: Muqātil reports that the Prophet said one hardship will not overcome two eases and recited this verse.
RAZI:94:6/r3.anchor: عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال :  " لن يغلب عسر يسرين "

RAZI:94:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
RAZI:94:6/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj take definite al-ʿusr as generic and thus one hardship in both clauses, while the indefinite yusr denotes two distinct eases.
RAZI:94:6/r4.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : العسر مذكور بالألف واللام

RAZI:94:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r5.speaker: الجرجاني
RAZI:94:6/r5.claim: Al-Jurjānī rejects that grammatical inference: repeating a phrase about one knight and a sword does not entail two swords.
RAZI:94:6/r5.anchor: وزيف الجرجاني هذا وقال : إذا قال الرجل

RAZI:94:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:94:6/r6.claim: The second clause may repeat the first to establish its meaning firmly, as the repeated warning in 77:15 does.
RAZI:94:6/r6.anchor: ويكون الغرض تقرير معناها في النفوس وتمكينها في القلوب

RAZI:94:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:94:6/r7.claim: On this reading, the two eases are worldly success in opening lands and the afterlife's reward in Paradise, as in the two good outcomes of 9:52.
RAZI:94:6/r7.anchor: يسر الدنيا وهو ما تيسر من استفتاح البلاد

RAZI:94:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:94:6/r8.claim: The indefinite form of yusr magnifies it: the promise is of an immense, remarkable ease.

RAZI:94:6/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:94:6/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:94:6/r9.claim: Although hardship and ease are opposites, ease follows hardship after a short interval so certainly that it is treated as accompanying it.
RAZI:94:6/r9.anchor: لما كان وقوع اليسر بعد العسر بزمان قليل

TAB:94:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:94:6/r1.claim: The hardship is the Prophet’s struggle with the polytheists; alongside it is hope and relief, namely victory until they submit to the truth willingly or unwillingly.
TAB:94:6/r1.anchor: رجاءً وفرجا بأن يُظْفِرَك بهم ،   حتى ينقادوا للحقّ الذي جئتهم به طوعا وكَرها

TAB:94:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:6/r2.speaker: النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:94:6/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reports that when the verse was revealed the Prophet told his companions to rejoice: ease had come, and one hardship would not overcome two eases; Qatada also relays this saying. No grading is stated.
TAB:94:6/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «أبْشِرُوا أتاكُمُ اليُسْرُ ،   لَنْ يَغْلِبَ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَيْنِ »

TAB:94:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:6/r3.speaker: النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:94:6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Prophet once came out joyful and laughing, repeating that one hardship would not overcome two eases and reciting the verse twice; no grading is stated.
TAB:94:6/r3.anchor: عن الحسن ،   قال :  خرج النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما مسرورا فَرِحا وهو يضحك ،   وهو يقول :  «لَنْ يَغْلِبَ عُسْرٌ يُسْرَيْنِ

TAB:94:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:6/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB:94:6/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says that if hardship entered a burrow, ease would follow it inside, appealing to God’s repeated promise; no grading is stated.
TAB:94:6/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود ،   قال :  لو دخل العسر في جُحْر ،   لجاء اليسر حتى يدخل عليه ،   لأن الله يقول

TAB:94:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:94:6/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:94:6/r5.claim: Mujahid explains that ease follows hardship.
TAB:94:6/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  إنّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرا قال :  يتبع اليسرُ العُسرَ

ITQAN:v3p177/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p177/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p177/r6.claim: A repeated sentence is best introduced by thumma, as in repeated warnings about Judgment Day and you will know.

BAQILLANI:v1p105/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r3.claim: Repetition is a recognized poetic figure, and the Quran similarly repeats the assurance that with hardship comes ease.
BAQILLANI:v1p105/r3.anchor: هلا سألت جموع كندة يوم ولوا أين أينا

BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.claim: When the same definite noun is repeated, the second usually refers to the first; examples include hardship in 94:5–6, the path in the Fatiha, and celestial objects in 41:37.
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.anchor: فالأول إن يكونا معرفتين والثاني فيه هو الأول غالبا

BURHAN:v4p93#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r2.speaker: التنوخي
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r2.claim: Al-Tanukhi explains that the hardship is one because the definite article denotes the unique generic kind, which is neither individually one nor numerically many.
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r2.anchor: قال التنوخي إنما كان مع العسر واحدا لأن اللام طبيعة لا ثاني لها بمعنى إن الجنس هى

BURHAN:v4p97/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p97/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p97/r2.claim: A common account says the repeated indefinite “ease” is distinct from the first, whereas the definite “hardship” refers back; some explain the indefinite as generic and the definite as already known.
BURHAN:v4p97/r2.anchor: والمشهور في تمثيل هذا القسم اليسر في قوله تعالى ﴿ فإن مع العسر يسرا إن مع العسر يسرا ﴾

BURHAN:v4p97/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p97/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p97/r3.claim: The author concludes that the second sentence emphasizes the first rather than promising two separate eases: explicit repetition implants the point, just as repeating “Zayd has a book” does not imply two books.
BURHAN:v4p97/r3.anchor: والتحقيق إن الجملة الثانية هنا تاكيد للاولى لتقديرها في النفس وتمكينها من القلب ولانها تكرير صريح لها

BURHAN:v4p97/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p97/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p97/r6.claim: The same repetition question appears in legal theory: repeating “Pray two units” may be a second command for a second act or merely emphasis; jurists hold both views.
BURHAN:v4p97/r6.anchor: واعلم انه ينبغي إن ياتي في هذا القسم الخلاف الاصولي في نحو صل ركعتين صل ركعتين

BURHAN:v2p386/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p386/r4.claim: Repetition also occurs in an adverbial expression and in complete clauses; the repeated clause إن مع العسر يسرا serves as emphasis.
BURHAN:v2p386/r4.anchor: ويكون في اسم الفعل كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p386/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p386/r5.claim: The second إن مع العسر يسرا, repeated for emphasis, is absent from Ibn Masʿūd's codex and recitation.
BURHAN:v2p386/r5.anchor: الجملة الثانية للتوكيد سقطت من مصحف ابن مسعود ومن قراءته

ITQAN:v2p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p560/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p560/r4.claim: The repeated definite hardship refers to the same hardship, while the indefinite ease is different; the Prophet therefore said one hardship will not overcome two eases.
ITQAN:v2p560/r4.anchor: فالعسر الثاني هو الأول واليسر الثاني غير الأول ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في الآية لن يغلب عسر يسرين
